purpose: Extend the Step 200 sleeve to the full 1993-2026 span, report the leverage grid without selecting a point, and test whether conditional volatility targeting improves the shape at lower turnover than the unconditional rule.
the_1993_caveat: Before 2007 the universe is not cross-asset. SPY exists from 1993, sector ETFs from 1998, QQQ from 1999, bonds from 2002, gold from 2004. A pre-2007 result is therefore a measurement of a progressively smaller and more equity-concentrated universe, and any comparison against the 2007+ figures conflates the rule with the opportunity set. Both are reported; neither is presented as the headline.

declared_before_running.signal: mean sign of total return over each lookback; hold only assets with positive score
declared_before_running.sizing: inverse trailing 126d volatility within the held set, scaled to a portfolio volatility target
declared_before_running.rebalance: last trading day of each calendar month

variants.unconditional: Scale to the volatility target at every rebalance.
variants.conditional: Scale only when trailing realised portfolio volatility exceeds the target; otherwise hold the unscaled inverse-volatility book capped at the leverage cap.
variants.no_vol_target: Inverse-volatility weights with no portfolio-level scaling, as a control that isolates what the targeting itself contributes.

questions: Does the Sharpe hold up before 2007, and if not, is that the rule failing or the universe shrinking?
Does the conditional variant match the unconditional one on drawdown at lower turnover?
Is the Sharpe still close to invariant across the leverage grid, which is what makes the sleeve scalable?
not_claimed: No point on the leverage grid is selected. Choosing one after seeing the grid converts a structural test into a fitted one.
This remains a probe. No forward clock is started and nothing is promoted.
Pre-2007 figures are not comparable to post-2007 figures and are not averaged with them.
